message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to not want to share an Animal Crossing town with my girlfriend. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, there's this new Animal Crossing game coming out, and each Nintendo Switch console can only have one village. My girlfriend and I both have our own Switches, but she wants to share one village with me. That means we'd both use one Switch to play the game together. I, on the other hand, would rather both of us get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want. I even offered to buy her the game, but she refused. She said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in Animal Crossing, which I just don't get. When I insisted on playing on different consoles, even after explaining my reasons, she got really upset. She stormed out, called me a asshole, and told me to grow up. Now, I'm feeling conflicted. I love the Animal Crossing series, and I want to be able to make my village the way I want. I also want to be able to play with my girlfriend online. Is it wrong of me to want to have my own game and customize my town the way I want? Or is it wrong of her to insist on sharing one village and not understanding my desire for personalization and online play? Maybe I should think about why she wants to share a village. She mentioned feeling a sense of togetherness, which is important in a relationship. But I also have my own interests and preferences. Is there a way to compromise? Perhaps we could spend some time playing together on one Switch and some time playing separately on our own Switches. That way, we both get to experience the game in the way we prefer. But I'm not sure if she would agree to that. I also wonder if there's a deeper issue here about our communication and understanding of each other's needs. It seems like she values the shared experience more, while I value the personalization and flexibility of having my own game. Maybe I should talk to her again and try to find a middle ground. It's important to respect each other's interests and find a solution that works for both of us. But I'm still hurt by her reaction, and I'm not sure how to approach her about this without things getting heated again. In the end, I think it's not inherently wrong to want to have your own game and customize your town the way you want. It's also not wrong for her to want to feel connected through the game. The challenge is finding a balance that respects both of our preferences. I guess the key is open communication and trying to understand each other's perspectives. If we can do that, maybe we can find a solution that works for both of us and strengthen our relationship in the process.
